Title: Diagnosis of test `testNodeSetOperations`

Details:
The test `testNodeSetOperations` contains a call to `assertXPathValue(context, "$array > 0", Boolean.TRUE, Boolean.class)` on line 100. This test is verifying that the XPath expression `$array > 0` evaluates to `Boolean.TRUE`.

The assertion method called is `assertXPathValue(JXPathContext ctx, String xpath, Object expected, Class resultType)`. This method (from `org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathTestCase`) disables lenient mode on the XPath context, calls `ctx.getValue(xpath, resultType)` and asserts that the result equals the expected value.

The key operation happens in `JXPathContext.getValue(String xpath, Class requiredType)`. This is an abstract method, so the actual evaluation occurs in a concrete implementation. Since this is testing XPath expressions with node set operations like `$array > 0`, the evaluation of the expression with the operator `>` on a node set `$array` and constant `0` is likely implemented in the internal compiler classes, possibly in or related to `CoreOperation` or its subclasses.

The failure indicates that the evaluation of `$array > 0` did not produce `Boolean.TRUE` as expected, likely because the node set operation is not properly handled in the evaluation. This can be due to the `CoreOperation` subclass that implements the `>` (greater-than) operator incorrectly handling comparison between node sets and constants.

No direct code for evaluation logic in `CoreOperation` or its subclasses was found in the snippets searched. The abstract `getValue` method is probably called on an expression tree that includes `CoreOperation` nodes.

Conclusion:
The bug likely arises because the operation that evaluates relational operators (such as `>`) on node sets does not correctly handle the case when `$array` is a node set, resulting in an incorrect boolean evaluation. The assertion fails since the actual evaluated value does not match the expected `Boolean.TRUE`.

The correct fix should be in the method responsible for evaluating the `>` operator (or other relational operators) in the XPath evaluation, particularly when at least one operand is a node set.
